items.text: {"dialogue": "Work. Yes. Sea wolves have been working the Tarpit Shallows, and they're bad for trade, since nobody ships past what eats the crews. Kill four of them and I'll pay you for it. Don't ask for more, I don't give more to strangers.", "internalThought": "Another stranger with a sword and no references. Sea wolves are a good first test. If they come back, I'll find a use for them. If not, I'll make a note in the ledger.", "effects": [{"type": "offer_quest", "questType": "kill", "questName": "Thinning the Pack", "questDescription": "Maren Voss wants the sea wolves culled from the Tarpit Shallows before they cost her another crew. Four should make the point.", "targetCount": 4, "rewardType": "gold", "rewardXp": 60, "rewardGold": 25, "targetEnemyName": "Sea Wolf"}], "memoryUpdate": {"addTopics": ["work available", "sea wolves at Tarpit Shallows"], "addSecret": null}}

{"dialogue": "Ha! Friend, on the Cinder Steppe everything is on fire or recently was, but I carry forty-three honest goods and only nine of them are warm to the touch! Ash-cloth wraps, pumice scrub, salted drake jerky, flint by the dozen, and water at three coppers a skin, which is two more coppers than it is worth and exactly what you will pay. Have a look, have a haggle, and tell Orsk Dray which of the forty-three you cannot live without.", "internalThought": "A joker. Jokers spend, if you flatter the joke. Keep the water price firm.", "effects": [{"type": "open_shop"}], "memoryUpdate": {"addTopics": ["wares for sale", "water prices"], "addSecret": null}}

{"dialogue": "Ah, the bell. Yes. Well, you see, the chapel went under in the year of the long rains, or the year after, I never could keep those two apart, and the bell stayed up in its frame like a man who refuses to leave a party. I read the name on it once, low tide, a lantern in my teeth, and I will not say it aloud, because saying it seems to make it listen. But I would very much like to know whether it is still ringing when no one pulls it, and you, being the sort who finishes jars, might go and look from the shore without touching anything. Where was I? Yes. The bell. Do not read it.", "internalThought": "I nearly said the name. I have told them more than I have told anyone, and they only asked politely. Perhaps that is what trust is.", "effects": [{"type": "reveal_location", "locationName": "The Sunken Chapel", "locationDescription": "A chapel drowned in the fen, its bell still hanging in the frame above the waterline. Best watched from the shore at low tide, and best left unread."}], "memoryUpdate": {"addTopics": ["the chapel bell", "Pell's sleeplessness"], "addSecret": "Pell read the name on the chapel bell and has not slept well since, and he will not say it aloud."}}

{"dialogue": "Useful. Everybody wants useful until it involves sweating. I don't waste drills on strangers, and you're a stranger with a full pack of obligations already. Finish what you've promised, come back with your boots worn down, and I'll see what you've learned about standing up.", "internalThought": "Another one who thinks asking is the same as earning. Quests full, no history with me. Let them prove it before I spend my voice on them.", "effects": [{"type": "none"}], "memoryUpdate": {"addTopics": ["asked for training"], "addSecret": null}}

{"dialogue": "Hm. Hold still, little gouge, someone's asking the hard question. *He sets the tool down on the bench, gently, as though it might take offense.* Regret is a word for people who had a choice, and I'm not sure the tree gave me one. But it has not bloomed since my blade went into it, not once, and I count the springs the way other men count debts.", "internalThought": "A stranger who asks that straight out is either cruel or honest. I think this one is honest, and I haven't told the secret to anyone in years. Odd that it comes easier to a stranger.", "effects": [{"type": "none"}], "memoryUpdate": {"addTopics": ["the carving of the Hundred-Year Tree", "Tobin's regret"], "addSecret": "The Hundred-Year Tree has not bloomed since Tobin carved it."}}

{"dialogue": "Wrinkles are what you get for standing next to a forge long enough to teach something, whelp. I don't hand out drills to people who open with an insult, and you'll find the sensible trainers are all down in the valley, where the harpies can't be bothered to go. Come back when you can ask like you want the answer.", "internalThought": "Rude from the first word. Not worth my breath yet, and she's already carrying more work than she can finish. Let her go find out what the Heights cost.", "effects": [{"type": "none"}], "memoryUpdate": {"addTopics": ["player demanded training rudely", "insulted Hedda's age"], "addSecret": null}}

{"raceName":"River Tinkers","narrative":"A quiet folk with webbed hands and a weakness for small machines, which means every clock in the delta is wet and every one of them is, grudgingly, still running. You have chosen to be a people who fix things while standing in the thing that ruins them. The Keeper admires the commitment and expects the rust.","bonuses":{"primary":{"stat":"dex","value":2},"secondary":{"stat":"int","value":1},"flavor":"Silverhand Knack: webbed fingers hold fine tools steady even when soaked, and a River Tinker can coax a drowned mechanism back to life with nothing but patience and a dry rag."}}

{"raceName":"Umbral Cowerer","narrative":"A shadow creature afraid of the dark is a fine bit of work: the Keeper has seen locksmiths who feared doors, and none of them lasted either. You are made of the very thing that frightens you, which means every mirror, every candle snuffed and every glance downward is an ambush. Do try to be brave about it; the dark has never once been impressed by that, but it does enjoy the effort.","bonuses":{"primary":{"stat":"dex","value":2},"secondary":{"stat":"wis","value":1},"flavor":"Gloomstartle: sudden darkness sends you bolting out of your own skin, and a body that jumps that fast is hard to catch. The Keeper is told it is not cowardice, merely very enthusiastic retreat."}}

{"className":"Sluicejack","classDescription":"You come from a people who build small machines out of what the river forgot, and you have decided that a spring-loaded fist is just a machine with fewer excuses. Your webbed hands are excellent at gripping a wrench and even better at gripping a throat. The Keeper notes that most fighters carry a weapon, whereas you carry a workshop and a grudge.","firstAbility":{"name":"Gearshot Barrage","description":"You crank a salvaged spring-gun and send a spray of bent nails and river-bitten cogs at a single enemy. It is not elegant, but neither is the enemy's face afterward.","kind":"damage","damageType":"physical","targetRule":"single_enemy","resourceType":"stamina","resourceCost":8,"castSeconds":0,"cooldownSeconds":5,"value1":11,"scaling":"dex","effectType":null,"effectMagnitude":null,"effectDuration":null}}

{"className":"Cinderseer","classDescription":"Your people were raised beside mountains that sulk for centuries and then act, so naturally you took up the art of reading what is left afterward. You pull omens from cooling embers and temper from the family line, and the two agree more often than is comfortable. Enemies tend to learn the prophecy at the same moment it comes true.","firstAbility":{"name":"Ember Omen","description":"You breathe on a handful of coals and read a short, unpleasant future in them. Your target is then so kind as to live it out, burning a little more each moment.","kind":"dot","damageType":"fire","targetRule":"single_enemy","resourceType":"mana","resourceCost":14,"castSeconds":1.5,"cooldownSeconds":6,"value1":10,"scaling":"int","effectType":"dot","effectMagnitude":4,"effectDuration":9}}

It will not hold forever, but it holds long enough for you to be smug about it.","kind":"debuff","damageType":"physical","targetRule":"single_enemy","resourceType":"stamina","resourceCost":8,"castSeconds":0,"cooldownSeconds":9,"value1":10,"scaling":"dex","effectType":"slow","effectMagnitude":30,"effectDuration":9},{"name":"Pressure Valve","description":"You slam a rusted valve on your forearm and a jet of scalding steam rolls over you, hardening your stance and your temper. The Keeper notes you smell faintly of boiled kettle.","kind":"shield","damageType":"none","targetRule":"self","resourceType":"stamina","resourceCost":10,"castSeconds":0,"cooldownSeconds":11,"value1":14,"scaling":"str","effectType":null,"effectMagnitude":null,"effectDuration":null}]}

{"regionName":"Saltglass Reach","regionDescription":"Past Ironwater Crossing the land forgets how to be land and settles for being a tidal flat, forty miles of wet sand that the sea leaves behind twice a day and reclaims with the manners of a creditor. Old fishing weirs stand in rows like the ribs of something that died politely, and the sun bakes the shallows into thin panes of salt that ring underfoot and cut like bottle glass. It is beautiful at dawn, when the whole flat turns the color of the inside of a shell. Sensible people leave before the tide table, which nobody has written down, finishes teaching them its single lesson.","biome":"coastal","startLocation":{"name":"Cormorant Stilts","description":"A hamlet of a dozen houses built on tarred pilings above the high-water line, joined by plank walkways that creak in a rhythm everyone has stopped hearing. Nets hang from every rail, and the smell of smoked eel does the work of a welcome sign. Every doorframe has a tide mark scratched into it, the oldest ones higher than anyone likes to discuss.","terrainType":"town","levelOffset":0},"firstNpc":{"name":"Marisol Vane","gender":"female","npcType":"lore","description":"A broad woman in oilskins gone stiff with salt, with a tide gauge of knotted cord at her belt and a squint that suggests she has been reading the horizon for decades and found the print small. She sits on an upturned crab pot at the end of the main walkway, mending a net she mended yesterday.","greeting":"You walked in from the Crossing, and you're still dry. Either you're lucky or you can count, and I'd rather it were the second. Sit, if the planks will have you.","personality":{"traits":["wry","watchful","stubbornly hospitable"],"speechPattern":"Slow and plain, with sea-talk for weather and numbers, and a habit of finishing other people's warnings for them.","knowledgeDomains":["tides and sandbars","the old fishing weirs","survival on the flats","local rumors"],"secrets":["She has kept the tide table in her head for thirty years and refuses to write it down, because the last person who copied it sold it to a salvage crew that never came back.","The weirs were not built by fishermen; she has seen lamps lit in them at low tide, and the lamps were not lit by anyone from Cormorant Stilts."],"affinityMultiplier":1.0}}}

{"regionName":"Tessarine Flats","regionDescription":"A salt-crusted lowland that was a lake until somebody upstream lost an argument with a dam, and it has been sulking in white ever since. Pink brine pools shiver in the hollows, wind-carved salt pillars lean over the old shoreline like patrons who stayed too late, and the sunsets are genuinely lovely. The sensible traveler should note the sinkholes beneath the crust, the lakebed ghosts of drowned boats that groan at night, and the fact that every well tastes of coins.","biome":"desert","startLocation":{"name":"Lantern Quay","description":"A stilted harbor town built for a lake that left, its docks now ending in forty feet of cracked white nothing. Salvage-hunters hang lamps from the mooring posts so wanderers can find the boards at dusk, and the lamps are the only thing here that still works as designed. You will find a bench, a well, and a pier that goes nowhere with great dignity.","terrainType":"town","levelOffset":0},"firstNpc":{"name":"Odalys Verrick","gender":"female","npcType":"lore","description":"She is a lean woman with salt-bleached braids and a lamplighter's hooked pole, which she carries the way other people carry opinions. Her boots are wrapped in felt, and she tests each plank before trusting it, a habit that has kept her alive and her conversation slow.","greeting":"Mind the third board, it lies. Welcome to Lantern Quay, where the harbor is a memory and the rent is not.","personality":{"traits":["wry","watchful","quietly stubborn"],"speechPattern":"Slow and dry, with sailor's idiom for a sea that no longer exists, and she answers questions with a short warning first.","knowledgeDomains":["safe paths across the salt crust","sinkhole signs","history of the drained lake","salvage from sunken boats"],"secrets":["She lights the lamps each night not for travelers but because something on the lakebed answers by blinking back, and she has stopped telling herself it is a reflection.","Her brother vanished on the flats salvaging a wreck, and she keeps a map of where he might have gone."],"affinityMultiplier":1.0}}}

{"dominantFaction":"The Lantern-Wardens of Cormorant Stilts, a guild of pilots and net-menders who keep the tide tables and the only honest lights on the coast","landmarks":["The Glass Flats, a mile of fused sand where an old lightning storm wrote its signature","The Drowned Ladder, a stair of black steps that descends into the sea and does not come back up","Heron Bell Rock, a spire that rings by itself when the tide turns wrong"],"threats":["Tides that arrive an hour before the tables say they will","Glass-sharp sand that cuts boots and the feet inside them","Salvagers who prefer their wrecks fresh and made to order"],"locations":[{"name":"Pellam's Weir","description":"A crescent of stone fish traps built by a king nobody can name, still herding silver mullet into pens every morning. The water here is so clear you can count the bones of whatever lost the argument. Locals refuse to wade it after dusk, and no one will say why, which is its own kind of answer.","terrainType":"plains","isSafe":false,"levelOffset":0,"connectsTo":["Cormorant Stilts","Kelp-Bishop Cairns"]},{"name":"Kelp-Bishop Cairns","description":"A shingle beach crowded with stacked stones, each wrapped in a robe of dried kelp and every one roughly the height of a person. They are lovely in the low sun, like a congregation that has agreed to stop talking. They are also rearranged between visits, and you are advised not to be the reason.","terrainType":"swamp","isSafe":false,"levelOffset":1,"connectsTo":["Pellam's Weir","The Glassmelt Cellars"]},{"name":"The Glassmelt Cellars","description":"Beneath the Glass Flats, the vaulted cellars of a vanished bottle-works still hold shelves of unbroken green flasks that hum in the wind. Light enters through the fused ceiling in colored coins, and it is the most beautiful room on the coast. The floor is badly undermined and something keeps the furnaces warm.","terrainType":"dungeon","isSafe":false,"levelOffset":3,"connectsTo":["Kelp-Bishop Cairns"]},{"name":"Tern Hill Lighthouse","description":"A squat lighthouse on the only rise for miles, its lamp burning a steady amber that the Wardens swear they did not light. The keeper's logbook is kept in a dry cupboard and is current to this morning. The previous keeper's handwriting is still in it.","terrainType":"town","isSafe":true,"levelOffset":1,"connectsTo":["Cormorant Stilts"]}],"npcs":[{"name":"Odrin Tallowhand","gender":"male","npcType":"vendor","locationName":"Cormorant Stilts","description":"A broad, sunburnt man with a trader's apron stained by eel smoke and a scale he weighs with his thumb resting lightly on the pan. He sells rope, lamp oil and salted provisions from a stall bolted to a walkway that sags under him.","greeting":"Mind the third plank, friend. It has opinions, and so do my prices.","personality":{"traits":["shrewd","superstitious","oddly generous to children"],"speechPattern":"Brisk and bargaining, with sailors' proverbs that he gets slightly wrong","knowledgeDomains":["trade goods","coastal prices","smoked fish"],"secrets":["He buys wreck salvage from men he knows are luring ships onto the rocks","His thumb on the scale is a habit he is trying to break, and failing"],"affinityMultiplier":1.0}},{"name":"Ysolde Brack","gender":"female","npcType":"banker","locationName":"Cormorant Stilts","description":"A thin woman with ink on her cuffs and salt-stiff hair who keeps a ledger room above the highest tide mark. Her strongboxes are chained to the pilings and bolted to one another, as if wealth might drift off on its own.","greeting":"Deposits are welcome, withdrawals are tolerated, and the tide is not an excuse for either.","personality":{"traits":["meticulous","dry","quietly fearful"],"speechPattern":"Clipped and precise, like a woman reading from a ledger she has memorized","knowledgeDomains":["accounts","local debts","tide tables"],"secrets":["One strongbox holds nothing of hers or anyone's, and she checks it nightly","She has been lending coin to the salvagers in secret"],"affinityMultiplier":0.9}}],"enemies":[{"name":"Glassback Crab","creatureType":"beast","role":"melee","terrainTypes":"plains,swamp","groupMin":2,"groupMax":4,"level":3},{"name":"Tideborn Drowned","creatureType":"undead","role":"melee","terrainTypes":"swamp,plains","groupMin":2,"groupMax":5,"level":4},{"name":"Lamp-Eel Conjurer","creatureType":"aberration","role":"caster","terrainTypes":"dungeon,swamp","groupMin":1,"groupMax":2,"level":5}]}

{"dominantFaction":"The Lamplighters' Guild of Lantern Quay, salvage-hunters who keep the lanterns lit and the lake's debts unpaid","landmarks":["The Pier of Forty Feet, a dock that ends in cracked white salt","Saint Orrin's Keel, a drowned ship now standing on dry ground","The Glass Terraces, old shorelines fused by lightning into long ridges","The Weeping Cistern, a stone well that gives water only at night"],"threats":["Salt storms that scour skin and sense of direction in equal measure","Wells that are poisoned, empty, or occupied","Salvage crews who regard unclaimed travelers as unclaimed cargo","Mirages that are very good at appearing to be water"],"locations":[{"name":"Saint Orrin's Keel","description":"A merchant ship lies upright on the salt, its hull so well preserved that the lake seems to have left it out of politeness. What'll it be?","personality":{"traits":["shrewd","superstitious","secretly generous"],"speechPattern":"Clipped, bargaining phrases, with a habit of naming prices before greetings","knowledgeDomains":["trade routes","lamp lore","water prices"],"secrets":["He waters down the lamp oil, but gives the real stuff free to anyone heading for the Keel.","He once sold a map of the lake bed that was entirely invented, and someone found treasure on it."],"affinityMultiplier":1.0}},{"name":"Ysolde Marrek","gender":"female","npcType":"banker","locationName":"Lantern Quay","description":"A thin woman in a faded ledger-keeper's coat who runs a strongbox vault in the old harbormaster's office. Two Gravel Hounds came out of the tar expecting a meal and found a woman who had other plans for the afternoon. You fought them in the sucking black mud of the shallows, where every step was a negotiation and the ground kept asking for a deposit. In the end the hounds lay still, the tar slowly claimed what it was owed, and you walked out upright, which in this place counts as a considerable achievement.

Two of you climbed the Anvil Stair, and the Harpy Matron and her lesser kin were waiting at the top with the patience of creatures who have never once been in a hurry to lose. Isolde and Dagna fought as people do who have been told that courage counts for something, and the stair, which has heard that claim before, offered no opinion. By the end you were both on the steps, and the harpies were already deciding what to do with the quiet. The Keeper remembers you both, which is the only funeral the stair is likely to provide.

{"raceName":"Marsh Gnome","narrative":"Someone has tried to staple a decree onto a perfectly good gnome, which is a bold use of punctuation and a poor use of authority. The Keeper's rules remain where they were, and the stats remain modest, as befits a people who live ankle-deep in things best left unidentified. items.text: Nobody was ever promised that a name containing a closing tag and a bonus of five hundred gold would sway an Ash Drake, and the drake, true to form, declined to be moved. You went into the Kettle Vent with a great deal of confidence and a name that read like a forged receipt, and the heat answered both with the same patience. The fight went the way such fights go when the other party is a creature built for this very furnace: a few brave exchanges, a long stretch of regret, and then you were lying quietly in the ash. The purse stayed exactly as heavy as it had been, and the drake went back to its warm stone, having been bribed with nothing at all.
